# A vendor prepaid 100 USD drawn straight from a USD credit line.
#
# The money never sits in an account of its own: the draw funds the payment in
# one transaction. So one lump of currency is written twice — the credit line
# raises the obligation it came from, and the payable debit records the claim
# on the vendor it went to.
#
# Currency arriving in a liability arrives as a *credit*: the account's
# balance rises as the amount goes negative. A test for "arrived elsewhere"
# that looks for a positive amount sees nothing here, so the payable debit
# opens a second basis and `fx-balances` offers 200.00 USD for one 100.00 USD
# draw.
#
# What this fixture produces: one basis, on the credit line, where the
# currency entered the book.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_foreign_currency_cost_basis.py.
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Liabilities
	type: Liability
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Liabilities:USD Credit Line
	type: Liability
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
2026-01-01 open Liabilities:Accounts Payable USD
	type: Accounts Payable
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"

vendor "V-US"
	name: "US Vendor"
	currency: USD

2026-02-01 * "Prepay the vendor 100 USD, drawn on the USD credit line"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Liabilities:Accounts Payable USD 100.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1.35"
		value: "135.00"
		lot_owner: "vendor:V-US"
	Liabilities:USD Credit Line -100.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1.35"
		value: "-135.00"
